slides.heading: elif Chains
slides.body: elif Chains is part of Conditional Execution. This short lesson gives you a practical Python idea you can understand, try, and reuse in simple programs.

slides.heading: Core Idea: elif Chains
slides.body: An elif chain checks several conditions in order. Python runs the first matching branch and skips the rest.

slides.heading: Real-World Analogy
slides.body: elif is like choosing from several doors. The first door that fits the condition is opened.

slides.body: A conditional needs a colon, correct indentation, and a condition that clearly evaluates to True or False.

slides.heading: Try It Yourself!
slides.prompt: Use if-elif-else to classify a temperature as Hot, Warm, or Cold.
slides.hint: Check the highest condition first, then the next.

quiz.prompt_text: What does Python do once it finds a True condition in an elif chain?

options: It checks all remaining conditions anyway
It runs only the first matching branch and skips the rest
It returns to the start of the chain

quiz.explanation: Exactly right! Python runs only the first True branch in an elif chain and immediately skips the rest. This is called short-circuit evaluation.

quiz.prompt_text: Arrange the following lines to classify a grade as Excellent, Passed, or Review using elif.
quiz.explanation: The variable is first, then the if checks the highest threshold, its print block follows, then elif checks the next threshold with its block.

quiz.prompt_text: Use if-elif-else to classify a temperature: Hot for above 35, Warm for above 20, otherwise Cold.

content.hint: Check the highest condition first with if, then elif for the next, and else for the rest.

quiz.correct_answer: Any valid Python code that satisfies the prompt.
quiz.explanation: With temperature = 25: if temperature > 35: is False, elif temperature > 20: is True so Warm is printed. Always check the highest range first in elif chains.
